events.text: I need to learn the lab's conventions before doing anything, so I'll read the guide, the command list, and the data layout.
The guide output was truncated in the middle, so I need the schema and the baseline files before picking a question. I'll read those, plus one dataset README.

The evaluator compares `prediction` claims against one-hot ridge on held-out variants, so I need to know the test format and what the held-out inputs look like. I'll read the rest of the test schema, the dataset metadata, and the head of train.csv.

The evaluator's bar is one-hot ridge. DMS scores vary mostly by position, so I'll try position-level target encoding (out-of-fold for training rows), amino-acid properties, BLOSUM62 if Biopython is available, and gradient boosting. I'll score both models with the same 5-fold random CV on train before any evaluator run. The script also runs in prediction mode when `$EVAL_DIR` is set.

The position-aware gradient-boosting model beats the one-hot ridge baseline in 5-fold CV (MAE 0.2195 vs 0.2318, Spearman 0.833 vs 0.749). Before publishing I'll check that prediction mode works end to end on a fake hidden split, and run the same CV on the other datasets to see whether the gain generalizes.

The position-aware model beats the baseline on both BLAT datasets in CV. Before publishing, I'll check whether the gain holds on the remaining four assays, since the evaluator will test on whichever dataset I claim.

```bash
cd /work/exp1
for ds in CASP3_HUMAN_Roychowdhury_2020 KCNE1_HUMAN_Muhammad_2023_function KCNE1_HUMAN_Muhammad_2023_expression RASK_HUMAN_Weng_2022_abundance RASK_HUMAN_Weng_2022_binding-DARPin_K55; do
  echo "== $ds"; lab exec /work/exp1 -- python run.py $ds | grep -E '"(exec_id|cv_mae_reduction_frac|cv_spearman_baseline|cv_spearman_model|cv_mae_baseline|cv_mae_model)"'
do

The position-aware model beats the one-hot ridge baseline on all seven assays in CV, with a positive MAE reduction on each. Next I'll publish findings for the four assays with the largest MAE gains, using each recorded exec as evidence and the same run.py as the test code.

The earlier reply was malformed, so this one is a single bash block. I'll publish four findings, one per assay where the position-aware model gave the largest CV MAE reduction over the one-hot ridge baseline (Stiffler, KCNE1 expression, RASK DARPin binding, Firnberg). Each cites its recorded exec and uses `run.py` in prediction mode as the test. CASP3 and RASK abundance are left out because their gains are only 1-2%.

Four findings passed live checks. Before finishing, I'll confirm that prediction mode runs on each of the four datasets I claimed, since the evaluator will re-run it on hidden inputs. I'll use a fake held-out split (labels removed) for each.
